title: The Philosophy of April, 2026
author: Unknown Unknown
summary: This roundup article explores two significant themes in April 2026: the escalation of the war in Iran with massive spending on military hardware, and NASA's Artemis II lunar mission marking humanity's return to space exploration beyond Earth. The author examines why philosopher Emanuele Coccia believes we can never really leave Earth, then argues against this position with reference to deep time and human capability. The piece also discusses the latest viral social media trend 'Zoom in for a sign,' exploring what it means and why people are doing it. The article meditates on the philosophical implications of seeking signs and meaning in the digital age, characteristic of Mini Philosophy's approach to extracting grand principles from small contemporary moments.
points: Two competing narratives define April: military escalation and spending versus space exploration ambitions, both involving massive human and technological effort. Emanuele Coccia's argument that we cannot leave Earth philosophically invites examination of what leaving Earth might mean and what counts as genuine transcendence. The viral 'Zoom in for a sign' trend reveals how humans in the digital age seek meaning, patterns, and signs in everyday moments and images. April represents both humanity's worst impulses toward conflict and best impulses toward exploration and discovery. The intersection of technology, meaning-making, and human striving creates philosophical questions about our era and aspirations.
quotes: It's been a busy month for the rocket industry.
Much of which was on rockets, missiles, and air defense systems.
Artemis II rumbled its way into a nearly ten-day voyage around the Moon.
On April 1, we got new photos of Earth from space.
